original_question: If G is a K_{r+1}-saturated graph on n vertices, must its spectral radius satisfy lambda(G) >= lambda(S_{n,r-1}), with equality only when G is isomorphic to S_{n,r-1}?
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's intended target very closely: it asks about n-vertex K_{r+1}-saturated graphs, uses the adjacency spectral radius notation λ(G), identifies the complete split graph S_{n,r-1} as the extremal candidate, and includes the paper's uniqueness-of-equality conclusion. This is the nearest official formulation in the paper, namely Conjecture 15 in Section 14.
missing_details: The paper's standing conventions that all graphs are finite, simple, undirected, and unweighted are implicit and should be stated to make the question fully stand-alone.
The term K_{r+1}-saturated should be defined explicitly: G contains no K_{r+1}, but for every nonedge e of G, the graph G+e contains a copy of K_{r+1}.
The operator λ(G) should be defined explicitly as the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix A(G), i.e. the adjacency spectral radius.

The graph S_{n,r-1} should be defined explicitly as the complete split graph on n vertices consisting of a clique of size r-1 and an independent set of size n-r+1, with all edges between the two parts present.
The integer quantifiers/range for n and r are left implicit in the draft; to be self-contained one should state that n and r are integers in the natural range for the problem (at least n ≥ r ≥ 2).

The draft does not explicitly say that the question is asking whether S_{n,r-1} is the unique minimizer of λ among all n-vertex K_{r+1}-saturated graphs, which is the structural content of the conjecture.
refined_question: For integers n and r with n ≥ r ≥ 2, let S_{n,r-1} be the complete split graph on n vertices obtained from a clique of size r-1 and an independent set of size n-r+1 by adding all edges between the two parts. If G is a simple n-vertex K_{r+1}-saturated graph—that is, G contains no copy of K_{r+1}, but G+e contains a K_{r+1} for every nonedge e of G—must the adjacency spectral radius λ(G)=λ1(A(G)) satisfy λ(G) ≥ λ(S_{n,r-1}), with equality if and only if G ≅ S_{n,r-1}?
justification: The draft is targeting the specific conjecture stated in Section 14 on the minimum spectral radius of saturated graphs, not the broader neighboring Problem 8. The match is exact in substance: Section 14 states the same lower bound for λ(G) on K_{r+1}-saturated graphs and the same unique equality case S_{n,r-1}. The only information needed to make your draft fully stand-alone comes from the paper's preliminary notation: λ(G) is the largest adjacency eigenvalue, and S_{n,k} is the complete split graph. Section 14 also supplies the definition of F-saturated used in the conjecture. So the right refinement is a self-contained restatement of Conjecture 15 with these preliminaries folded in, without broadening to the more general Problem 8.
